segments.he: עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת זוֹכֶה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מַאֲכָלוֹ בִּבְחִינַת
segments.en: The essential education [chinuch] of every person in the service of G-d is through the above-mentioned aspect in the above teaching [Likutay Moharan I:34] — through the light of the above-mentioned point. That is, one receives from the light of the Tzaddik's point — and afterward each one receives from his fellow — and afterward from himself: through speaking between oneself and one's Creator, and through this the point shines. And through this one binds one's heart to G-d, and all the shames and breaks — that is, evil loves and so on — are nullified, and one ascends from the profane to the holy. It is found that the essential education to enter into holiness is through the above-mentioned point — through hisbodidus and intimate conversation between oneself and one's Creator — for through this precisely the point shines. And through this one can rectify everything.

segments.he: מְבאָר בִּדְבָרָיו זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁיְּכוֹלִין לִזְכּוֹת עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת וְכִסּוּפִין לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה עוֹשֶׂה נְפָשׁוֹת וְכוּ'. וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּל מַאֲכָלוֹ בִּבְחִינַת לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים. כַּמְבאָר בְּהַתּוֹרָה אִית לָן בֵּירָא בְּדַבְרָא (בְּסִימָן ל"א):
segments.en: The summary is that a person must strive all his days to seek and search greatly, greatly after his lost things. For this is the essential teshuvah. And if one seeks and searches properly — certainly one will find. And even at the time when one does not yet merit to find — even so, through every effort and search, one has already found much. For no effort or seeking is ever lost at all, and certainly one has found what one has found through every single word and every effort and search — for leis re'usa tava d'is'avid [Aramaic: "no good desire is lost"]. And each one, according to one's greater share in the seeking and searching — praiseworthy is him and according to the effort is the reward. For each one, the more one has toiled and distressed oneself on account of the lost things, and striven to seek them and search for them in prayer and supplication and with yearning and longing and drawing close to Tzaddikim and the genuinely upright, and suffered humiliations and much bloodshed [i.e., suffering] on this account — so much more will one merit that one's lost things be returned to one in peace. And all this is in the power of the great Tzaddik, who always searches for all the lost things and strengthens the heart of each one not to despair in any way from seeking and searching for the lost things in prayer and supplication, and to yearn greatly after them and to await salvation always — and through this they will merit that through him all the lost things of all the world will be found, speedily in our days, Amen.

On account of the intensification of exile — whose essence is the exile of the soul, principally through the intensification of the above sadness, from which all troubles come, G-d spare us — therefore one must cry out greatly every day, and the essential voice of the crying is to merit to emerge from sadness, from grief to joy — as is expressed in the Hodu Psalm: "and they cried" and "and they rejoiced for they were stilled" — for one must cry greatly in order to merit joy, which is the essential thing. And therefore one needs every day hisbodidus and conversation and much crying and so on. But the essential thing is to strengthen oneself every day and every time in joy. As is written much in our discussions, and as is explained in its place in Likutay Moharan Tinyana 25 and elsewhere: the greatness of hisbodidus, and it concludes: "and the rest of all the day should be in joy" — as above.
